messages:
elaine: Quick design check — forms team is debating inline field errors vs. a top summary for the new Settings > Integrations form. leaning inline for contextuality but worried keyboard users might miss errors at the top. thoughts?

sam: I lean inline too. immediate feedback saves clicks. but we should make the error linkable/focusable from the summary so keyboard users can jump.

kevin: Agree with sam. If we use inline, add a condensed top summary only when there are 3+ errors, with links that move focus to the field. avoids noise for 1-2 small errors.

nina: A11y nit: ensure the inline error is aria-live polite and the summary uses role=alert when shown after submit so screen readers announce it. Also confirm visible focus styles when jumping.

morgan: Copy thought — for destructive toggles we also show a small inline confirmation note below the toggle ("This will disconnect X — changes are immediate"). If that fails validation later, the summary should say which action caused the block. keeps causality clear.

elaine: Good call. For required field markers, do we keep the asterisk + helper text, or rely on placeholder + inline error? current mock uses asterisk + subtle label.

kevin: Keep asterisk. It's the fastest signpost. But pair with an explicit "Required" label in the field description for complex forms. Avoid relying on placeholder text for required state — placeholders disappear and aren't accessible.

a11y-bot: Automated scan: Inline error color contrast (error label) 2.8:1 on current token — fails AA. Recommend 4.5:1 body text or stronger weight.

nina: Also ensure error icons have text alternatives (aria-hidden true for decorative icons) and errors appear in DOM order near the input.

morgan: UX trade: inline reduces back-and-forth, summary helps overview. Can we prototype hybrid: inline realtime for typed validation, but on submit show a sticky summary with links if there are multiple errors?

elaine: Prototype plan sounds good. Implementation questions: do we animate focus jump? want smooth but instantaneous for keyboard users.

sam: keep it instantaneous. animation can skip focus detection for screen readers. maybe a 0ms scrollIntoView + highlight fade for sighted users.

kevin: Small pattern for destruct-confirm: prefer a typed-confirm for irreversible deletes, but for toggles (disconnect integration) a single "Confirm" inline CTA + undo toast is sufficient. typed-confirm for anything that wipes data.

nina: Accessibility addition: if we do typed-confirm, ensure the input has aria-label and we trap focus within the modal; also provide a descriptive live region after action completes.

elaine: Action items: 1) morgan to prototype hybrid inline + summary (0.5 day). 2) dev to implement aria-live + focus-jump pattern and correct contrast (kevin + sam). 3) copy updates for destructive language (elaine). 4) accessibility sweep with a11y-bot after prototype. Anyone object?

morgan: +1 will drop a Figma prototype by EOD and add two states (1 error, 4+ errors).

sam: I'll coordinate with eng to reserve time for the focus behavior.

kevin: I'll raise the contrast token in the theme and add a small utils PR.

nina: I'll run the a11y checklist once the prototype lands.

elaine: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for followups. :thumbsup:
